latest_release.name: v5.4.1
latest_release.body:
DonSeTch v5.4.1

### Fixed

- **The updater downloads release assets over parallel ranges.** A single stream from the release
  CDN is throttled per connection on some networks — measured 4-28 KB/s while the same 40 MB asset
  came down at 200+ KB/s over several connections — so an upgrade that should take minutes gave up
  after twenty. The downloader now probes with one range request, splits what is missing across
  eight connections, resumes each segment on a stall, and keeps the buffer a resumable prefix for
  the next route; a server that ignores `Range` is streamed exactly as before. An asset below 2 MB
  still takes the streaming path.

detail.readme:
DonSeTch

The web tools your agent needs.
Search, fetch, crawl, and screenshot. One local Rust binary. No required API keys or accounts.

Install · Tools · Design · Proxies · Limits · Docs · Sponsor

Find a source, read the useful part, follow a link, check a claim. DonSeTch gives agents that web loop over MCP or from your terminal, with about 2,000 tokens of tool schemas. **Page reads launch no browser.** Real client profiles, learned routes, and embedded V8 handle the fetch. Chromium is used separately for screenshots. Search needs no model download. ## Start here ### 1. Install ```bash npm install -g donsetch donsetch doctor ``` The installer downloads a SHA256-verified release binary. No Rust toolchain needed. Linux, macOS, and Windows are supported.
Homebrew, Pi, DeepSeek Harness, or build from source | Install | Command | |---|---| | Homebrew · macOS/Linux | `brew tap dondai44423/donsetch && brew install donsetch` | | Pi native extension | `pi install npm:donsetch` | | DeepSeek Harness plugin | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:dondai44423/donsetch-dsh` | Pi and dsh register native tools. For source builds, platform requirements, Docker, or installer troubleshooting, see the [setup guide](docs/setup.md).
### 2. Connect your agent Add this to your MCP client's server configuration, then restart the client: ```json { "mcpServers": { "donsetch": { "command": "donsetch", "args": ["mcp", "--supervised"] } } } ``` Works with Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and other MCP clients. Configuration formats vary; `donsetch doctor --mcp` prints registration examples using the binary's absolute path. `--supervised` restarts the stdio daemon after a crash. Need an HTTP endpoint? Run `donsetch mcp --http --port 8765` and connect to `http://localhost:8765/mcp`. [HTTP setup and authentication →](docs/setup.md#http-transport) ### 3. Try it ```bash # Find sources. donsetch search "rust async cancellation" --intent code # Read the passages that answer. donsetch fetch https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html \ --focus "cancel a task" # Map a documentation site. donsetch crawl https://docs.python.org/3/ --mode map --topic asyncio ``` The CLI and MCP tools use the same engine. No account setup sits between install and first use. **Worth keeping in your toolkit? [Star the repo](https://github.com/dondai44423/donsetch).** It helps other agent builders find it. ## Four tools. One process. | Tool | Use it for | Useful controls | |---|---|---| | `web_fetch` | Pages, PDFs, structured site records, or up to 12 URLs at once | `must_contain`, `focus`, `toc`, `section`, `since_last` | | `web_search` | Ranked sources and evidence snippets, keyless by default | `intent`, `lang`, `max_results`, `read` | | `web_crawl` | A site map or a bounded crawl with resumable progress | `mode`, `focus`, `max_pages`, `resume` | | `web_screenshot` | A rendered PNG through an installed Chromium-family browser | `full_page`, `wait_ms`, `deadline_ms` | Your agent chooses what to read next. DonSeTch supplies the tools. ### Read less. Keep the evidence. Every view works over the extracted source, including PDFs and site adapters. You choose what comes back: | Question | Option | Response | |---|---|---| | “Does this page mention it?” | `must_contain` | Counts, sections, and excerpts for up to eight phrases or regexes. | | “Where is the answer?” | `focus` | Relevant passages, best first, with their section paths. | | “What's in this document?” | `toc` | Headings and section IDs, without the body. | | “Read that part.” | `section` | One section and its subsections. | | “What changed?” | `since_last` | Changes against your stored previous read, or `unchanged`. | | “Keep going.” | `offset` | Continue at the returned `next_offset`. | ```bash donsetch fetch https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html \ --must-contain with_capacity --must-contain amortized ``` Amounts match by value: `15M` can find `EUR 15 000 000`. An unread portion makes an absence check `unverified`; it does not become a false “not found.” Use `--links` when you need citation URLs. [Fetch views, search options, crawl budgets, and result formats →](docs/tools.md) ## Under the hood [Open the route map at full size →](assets/readme/fetch-route.svg) **The client stays consistent.** TLS, HTTP/2, headers, hints, and cookies belong to one identity. A clearance is spent by the identity that earned it. Successful identities and routes are learned per site. **JavaScript runs when it has a job.** A challenge can mint clearance in V8. An application shell can run its own program against a data-only DOM. Nothing is laid out or painted. When a successful content run reveals a reusable data request, the fetcher stores that request and replays it over HTTP on later encounters. A broken replay is discarded and re-learned. **Search ranks evidence.** Sources are selected by query type, merged by measured index independence, and ranked with BM25+, RM3, and a compiled linear model for the query types where it won validation. No LLM, embeddings, or model download. **PDFs use text and pixels together.** PDFium supplies glyphs and rendered pixels from the same document. DonSeTch uses both to recover reading order, tables, and forms. Scans and corrupt text regions can use optional OCR, with uncertainty marked. [Architecture, cache behavior, local state, and source map →](docs/architecture.md) ### Measured, with the conditions attached | Recorded fetch run · 15 Nov 2026 | Content | Median | |---|---:|---:| | Cold · 28 defended targets × 2 rounds · up to 3 attempts | **49/56** · curl **21/56** | **1.18 s** | | Learned state · same 28 targets × 3 rounds · no page cache · 3 s deadline | **69/84** | **0.98 s** | These are home-IP measurements, not a promise for every site or network. The cold run paired curl in the same window. The learned run is a different protocol, not a controlled speed comparison. Neither run used the new program/replay transport. [Method, failures, and the separate live-web field test →](docs/benchmarks.md) ## Proxies without the guesswork **You don't need one to start.** A proxy is useful when an engine rate-limits your IP or a site treats your network differently. ```bash # Add one proxy. Use your own host and credentials. donsetch proxy add 'socks5://user:pass@proxy.example:1080' # Verify the tunnel, exit IP, and latency. donsetch proxy check donsetch proxy list ``` Restart the MCP server after changing the pool. The important part is what uses it: | Tool | Default with a configured pool | Change it | |---|---|---| | Search | Uses pool lanes for engine requests | Automatic | | Crawl | Starts direct; later reads can spread across pool lanes | `donsetch proxy crawl off` disables pool use | | Fetch | Uses your own IP | `donsetch proxy fetch on` enables the pool | “Direct” here means outside the pool. A configured `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, or `ALL_PROXY` can still route that request. A failed configured proxy is reported; it does not silently fall back to your IP. **Crawl contacts the seed directly before pool lanes take over.** To keep a site entirely out of scope, use a [local deny rule](docs/rules.md). [HTTP/SOCKS5 formats, imports, credentials, environment proxies, and troubleshooting →](docs/proxies.md) ## Optional keys The default tools work without keys. Bring your own when you want an additional search provider or a paid fetch fallback. ```bash donsetch keys add tavily 'YOUR_KEY' donsetch keys add exa 'YOUR_KEY' donsetch keys default local # Keyless first; paid search as fallback. ``` Native search providers: Tavily, Exa, Serper, SerpApi, SerpBase, Brave Search, TinyFish, Parallel, and Bright Data. Other providers can use the [executable plugin interface](docs/tools.md#search-plugins). Bright Data uses separate zones for SERP search and Web Unlocker: ```bash donsetch keys add bd 'YOUR_TOKEN::YOUR_SERP_ZONE' donsetch keys add unlocker 'YOUR_TOKEN::YOUR_UNLOCKER_ZONE' ``` Unlocker runs after a local wall, only with a configured key. Attempts can cost money and are capped per day. [Zone setup, costs, and troubleshooting →](docs/brightdata.md) ## Know the limits | Situation | What happens | |---|---| | A page requires login | `wall.auth`. No sign-in, imported browser cookies, or stored login credentials. | | A human challenge remains | A named wall. No local hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA, Turnstile, or press-and-hold solver. An optional Unlocker may help. | | Content needs layout or canvas | The fetch stays a declared shell if the program cannot produce readable content. Use a screenshot for pixels. | | A read hits its size or time limit | Partial content or a named failure, with continuation information when available. | | Search sources refuse the request | Source status and an empty or degraded answer. No invented results. | | You repeatedly harvest a defended site | Pacing helps; IP bans can still happen. This tool is for research, not bulk collection. | For signed-in browsing or long, human-paced sessions, use a real browser driver such as [Bladebro](https://github.com/dondai44423/bladebro). Local processing still makes requests to the sites you ask for. Optional providers and proxies receive the traffic you route through them. [Security policy →](SECURITY.md) ## Configuration and upkeep ```bash donsetch config show # Values and where they came from. donsetch config show --markdown # Every supported setting. donsetch doctor --deep # Live network and provider checks. donsetch status # Version, keys, proxies, and cache. donsetch update # Update from GitHub Releases. donsetch rollback # Restore the previous version. ``` Settings live in `donsetch.toml`. Precedence: defaults → legacy environment → config file → `DONSETCH_
__`. Unknown keys and invalid values fail clearly. [Config paths, browser setup, Docker, HTTP transport, and troubleshooting →](docs/setup.md) ## Documentation | Guide | What's inside | |---|---| | [Setup](docs/setup.md) | Install choices, platform matrix, MCP, HTTP, Docker, config, and repairs. | | [Tools](docs/tools.md) | Reading views, search, crawling, screenshots, BYOK plugins, and result contracts. | | [Proxies](docs/proxies.md) | Pool routing, environment proxies, credential formats, and diagnostics. | | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | Fetch, search, extraction, PDF, state, and the code behind them. | | [Measurements](docs/benchmarks.md) | Benchmark conditions and the live-web field report. | | [Local rules](docs/rules.md) | Refuse a host before fetching and give the agent your instructions. | | [Bright Data](docs/brightdata.md) | Optional SERP and Web Unlocker setup. | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Development loop, tests, PRs, and releases. | ## Support the project


Good tools take work. Help keep this one independent.

If DonSeTch earns a place in your agent's toolkit, [give it a star](https://github.com/dondai44423/donsetch), share a useful example, or [report a reproducible bug](https://github.com/dondai44423/donsetch/issues). Code and documentation contributions are welcome.

Email with your product and proposed use; we'll discuss whether an integration belongs in DonSeTch and what it would involve.
